core_tradeoff: Only one equipped weapon operates at a time

trigger.condition: the active weapon advances through occupied weapon slots every 4 active-simulation seconds

effects.rotation_order: stable loadout order through occupied weapon slots; empty slots are skipped

pause_behavior.rule: Fabrication and other full-simulation pauses freeze phase time.

live_state_meter.meter: active weapon, remaining phase time, and next weapon
live_state_meter.hud_treatment: concise status pip or meter beside the relic slot

acquisition.method: found in a relic cache through map exploration

unlock.effect: Permanently adds the relic to the random relic-cache selection pool; it neither equips nor guarantees that relic.

acquisition.cache_opening: automatic on mech contact; freezes the complete gameplay simulation
acquisition.resolution: immediate install-or-sell; no relic inventory or deferred decision

rarity_and_weighting.selection_model: three distinct relics drawn without replacement from the currently unlocked pool and assigned to the three caches during generation

stacking_and_exclusivity.modifier_order: Relic-specific multipliers apply after the additive percentage modifiers supplied by mech traits, utilities, and PowerUps unless the relic explicitly replaces targeting or cadence.
overrides_or_replaces: weapon-slot activation (only one weapon active at a time)

behavior_registration.hook: weapon-slot activation gate and rotating phase
behavior_registration.registration_model: Relics are cross-cutting policies registered by stable relic ID. They modify well-defined hook points rather than scattering ID checks through every weapon.
behavior_registration.per_weapon_compatibility_manifest: produced from tests; states fully affected, partially affected with disclosed reason, or invalid. The initial design expects no invalid pairing.

rules.text: The active weapon advances through occupied weapon slots in stable loadout order every four active-simulation seconds. Empty slots are skipped.
Only the active weapon may begin new attacks, deal continuous or contact damage, apply new control, or create movement-triggered output.

The active weapon produces five times its otherwise final output rate. For discrete attacks this ordinarily means five times the activation frequency; continuous, contact, and distance-triggered weapons receive an equivalent visible output-rate mapping.

Finite projectiles, mines, fields, trails, and autonomous attacks created during an active phase remain present and finish their already-authored behavior after the source weapon rotates inactive, but they cannot begin new autonomous attack events while inactive.
The HUD shows the active weapon, remaining phase time, and next weapon. Fabrication and other full-simulation pauses freeze phase time.
The five-times factor intentionally makes the relic a raw-power increase with a severe coverage and timing constraint, including when fewer than four weapon slots are occupied.
